title: incremental-graph-slicing-and-shape-agnostic-priming-to-mitigate-warmup-flaps
author: Lena Kirov
release_notes: Introduce incremental CUDA Graph slicing with shape-agnostic priming and KV-cache alignment to reduce warmup regressions for mixed-length continuous batching workloads. Enabled behind runtime feature flag.
description:
Context and problem: We continue to see intermittent warmup regressions and 'shape-guard flaps' when CUDA Graph capture/replay is used with continuous batching on mixed-length request streams. On heavy fragmentation (many short + few long sequences) the current capture strategy either over-captures (producing many narrow graphs that thrash kernels) or under-primes (leading to replay misses and slow software fallback). This PR implements an alternative capture strategy that reduces capture churn and prevents warmup regressions while preserving the low-latency benefits of cudagraph replay.

Design summary: Implement incremental graph slicing with a shape-agnostic priming layer and KV-cache alignment. Key ideas: 1) Split long input batches into a small set of canonical "slices" (prefix lengths) determined by runtime probing heuristics; captures target slices instead of individual request shapes. 2) Introduce a lightweight priming pass that is shape-agnostic: it drives kernels with safe padded inputs to populate persistent kernel states and warmed-up CUDA contexts without requiring exact shape matches. 3) Align KV-cache shard boundaries to slice boundaries so that KV replay semantics remain valid across captures (avoids stale-offset regressions seen previously). 4) Scheduler integration: when fragmentary sequences arrive we coalesce them into slice groups for capture; we also add a small delay budget (configurable) to allow opportunistic coalescing. 5) Fallback: when priming fails or a new unseen extreme shape arrives we gracefully fall back to the deterministic path and schedule an asynchronous capture for the new slice.

Feature flag and rollout: Changes are guarded behind runtime flag "enable_incremental_graph_slicing" with per-tenant throttles and a safe default off. We added metrics and tracing hooks so SRE can ramp the flag progressively.

Why this is different from previous approaches: instead of trying to maintain exact shape guards for every observed sequence shape (which led to many small graphs and eviction churn), the slice-based approach amortizes captures across shapes while keeping the warmed kernel state relevant. The priming pass is conservative (pads to safe widths) and is designed to avoid kernel rewrites that would trigger unnecessary kernel migrations.

Benchmarks: On internal mixed-length chat workload: p50 token latency improved by 6% (from 33ms to 31ms), p95 improved by 18% (from 120ms to 98ms) with a 32% reduction in graph capture rate under steady state. CPU overhead for priming is under 2% of total scheduler CPU. When enabled on canary, observed warmup error rate dropped from ~3.2% of sessions to 0.4% (errors defined as requests hitting slow fallback path after capture miss).

Testing and validation: Unit tests for slice selection heuristics, integration tests for KV-cache alignment across captures, end-to-end soak tests on internal perf-canary with mixed-length traces. Added a regression test that replays a previously failing incident trace and asserts stable warmup within 3 captures. CI: initial runs hit a flaky test in kv-cache shard reconciliation; fixed and re-ran.

Checklist (completed): - [x] Design doc and review with runtime/serving teams - [x] Feature-flag gated implementation - [x] Unit + integration tests - [x] Microbenchmarks and canary runs - [x] Observability (metrics/tracing) added - [x] Documentation note in serving runtime changelog

Open items / follow-ups: 1) Consider a dynamic slice compaction job to merge rarely used slices and reduce memory overhead (tracked ENG-9221). 2) Explore kernel-level hints to the compiler to reduce padded-priming overhead (future work).

Commits summary: See commits list.

Changed areas: Major changes in serving/runtime/cudagraph manager and scheduler, kv-cache alignment codepaths, runtime feature flag plumbing, new metrics + tracing, and integration tests under perf-canary harness.

Merge rationale: Measured perf gains on canary and strong reduction in warmup regressions. Changes are behind flag and include robust fallback so rollout is low risk.

review_comments: Marcus Lee: This looks promising. Two questions: (1) how do we choose slice canonical lengths under rapidly shifting traffic? (2) can priming accidentally change kernel selection and cause regressions?

Author (Lena Kirov): For (1) we use a lightweight moving-window histogram and prefer recent hits with exponential decay; the window is configurable. For (2) priming pads to a conservative width and we explicitly avoid invoking backends that would select alternate kernels; see priming_pass.cc where we set 'kernel_hint=conservative'. Added a test that asserts no kernel-id changes on priming flows.
Priya Nair: Please ensure the feature flag supports per-tenant throttles (we need to roll back quickly). Also add a metric that counts priming-induced padding tokens so we can monitor overhead.
Author (Lena Kirov): Added per-tenant throttle config and priming_padding_tokens metric (serving/runtime/metrics/cudagraph_metrics.cc).
Ethan Ramirez: Observability is good. CI reported a flaky test in shard_alignment_test; request to add a deterministic reconciliation path for the unit test so it's stable.
Author (Lena Kirov): Rewrote the reconciliation unit test to use deterministic clocks and added the deterministic path guarded by 'test_mode' flag in shard_alignment_test.cc. CI green now.
